Severe hepatotoxicity has been associated with zafirlukast.1-4 The Canadian manufacturer reported4 in April 2004 that from worldwide postmarketing surveillance of zafirlukast there had been 46 reports of hepatitis, 14 of hepatic failure, 3 of which progressed to fulminant hepatitis, and 59 re- ports of other clinically significant hepatic dysfunction; 7 fatali- ties had occurred. In most, but not all, cases symptoms had abat- ed and liver enzymes had returned to normal after stopping zafirlukast. It was important that prescribers, patients and/or their carers were alert to the signs and symptoms of hepatotoxicity. Licensed product information for zafirlukast advises stopping treatment if hepatotoxicity is suspected, and performing liver function tests; 1. Grieco AJ, Burstein-Stein J.
